extraction.agency_name: Department of Business and Economic Development
extraction.parent_department: Department of Business and Economic Development

findings.title: Comprehensive Written Procedures Were Not Prepared to Ensure Consistency and Compliance with the Law in Administering the Auction
findings.description: DBED did not establish effective oversight of the Premium Tax Credit auction as it failed to ensure comprehensive written procedures were developed for the process. Additionally, tax credit certificates issued included incorrect identifying information.

dollar_amounts.context: proceeds from the auction
tax credits awarded to winning bidders
cumulative value difference between multi-price and single price award methods

findings.recommendation: DBED should ensure comprehensive written procedures are developed for significant programs, comply with State law provisions, and correct/reissue tax credit certificates.

findings.title: The Selection of Venture Firms and the Allocation of Capital Was Not Adequately Documented, and Monitoring Efforts Were Not Sufficient
findings.description: DBED did not adequately document the methodology used to select venture firms or allocate capital. Additionally, required investment reports were frequently missing or incomplete, and management fees were not monitored for compliance with legal limits.

dollar_amounts.context: designated for the Maryland Venture Fund
minimum capital allocated to selected venture firms
management fees paid during calendar year 2013
fees charged above the legal limit

findings.recommendation: DBED should adequately document selection methodology and capital allocation, ensure required reports are received and reviewed, and monitor management fees for accuracy and compliance.

findings.title: Investment Bank Accounts Were Not Properly Approved
findings.description: DBED opened four investment bank accounts without obtaining required approval from the Office of the State Treasurer in advance. Deposits totaled approximately $34.5 million and disbursements totaled $18.1 million during the period before approval.

dollar_amounts.context: deposits into the accounts
disbursements from the accounts

findings.recommendation: DBED should obtain required State Treasurer approval prior to establishing special bank accounts.

findings.title: DBED’s Process for Verifying That Recipients Met Requirements for Forgiveness of Conditional Loans and Grant Repayments Was Not Effective
findings.description: DBED forgave loans and grants based on recipient-reported data without verifying accuracy or ensuring required documentation was submitted. Between December 2010 and January 2015, $6.8 million in conditional loans and grants were forgiven.

dollar_amounts.context: total amount of conditional loans and grants forgiven
loan balance forgiven in testing sample
grant repayment requirements forgiven in testing sample

findings.recommendation: DBED should establish effective procedures for verifying employment data, increase verification reviews by OIA, and develop formal written procedures.

findings.title: Formal Procedures for the Use of Forbearance Agreements and an Effective Mechanism for Tracking Agreements Had Not Been Established
findings.description: DBED lacked formal procedures for using forbearance agreements when loans defaulted and did not have a mechanism to track or monitor these agreements. Four loans totaling approximately $434,000 were identified with multiple modifications.

dollar_amounts.context: loans with forbearance agreements modified multiple times
balance of one loan examined as example

findings.recommendation: DBED should establish formal procedures and criteria for forbearance agreements and maintain adequate loan records to track activity.

findings.title: User Capabilities for DBED’s Financing Programs System Were Not Adequately Restricted
findings.description: Employee capabilities to record critical transactions were not adequately restricted, and certain users had unnecessary access. One employee responsible for monitoring security settings was also capable of posting critical transactions.

dollar_amounts.context: financial instruments tracked on the system

findings.recommendation: DBED should ensure critical transactions are subject to supervisory review, restrict employee access to necessary levels only, and designate an independent supervisor for monitoring.

findings.title: Cash Balances for Financing Programs Were Not Adequately Reconciled to the State’s Records
findings.description: DBED did not adequately reconcile cash balances on its monitoring system with State records. As of January 2015, reconciliations were overdue and contained unresolved differences.

dollar_amounts.context: cash balance on the monitoring system
cash balance on State records
unresolved difference between balances

findings.recommendation: DBED should ensure monthly reconciliations are timely, investigate and resolve differences, and ensure reviews are documented by independent supervisory personnel.

findings.title: Applicants’ Compliance With Job Creation Requirements and Associated Costs Were Not Sufficiently Verified
findings.description: DBED did not sufficiently verify applicants' compliance with job creation requirements or associated costs. Credits totaling $54.7 million were issued during the audit period.

dollar_amounts.context: tax credits issued during audit period
credits issued to entities not meeting time requirements
project and start-up costs without documentation

findings.recommendation: DBED should verify new positions created, ensure adherence to time requirements in State law, and obtain detailed documentation for claimed costs.

findings.title: Required Program Regulations Were Not Established and DBED Lacked Documentation of Supervisory Reviews
findings.description: Regulations for the Film Production Activity Tax Credit program were not adopted as required. Additionally, there was a lack of documentation that supervisory personnel reviewed credits prior to issuance.

dollar_amounts.context: film production activity tax credits issued during fiscal years 2012 through 2014

findings.recommendation: DBED should adopt regulations in conjunction with the Comptroller and perform documented supervisory reviews of credit certificates.

findings.title: Award and Disbursement Procedures Were Not Adequate
findings.description: Controls over Maryland State Arts Council Grants were not sufficient due to inadequate documentation of award decisions, lack of separation of duties, and insufficient reconciliation. Funds totaling $4.7 million were disbursed before grant agreements were executed.

dollar_amounts.context: grant disbursements during fiscal year 2014
initial grant disbursements tested in sample
funds disbursed prior to agreement execution
disbursements approved before agreements executed

findings.recommendation: DBED should maintain formal meeting minutes, verify invoices to documentation, reconcile records periodically, and ensure agreements are executed before payment.

findings.title: Certain purchasing transactions and access to the State’s Financial Management Information System (FMIS) were not sufficiently controlled.
findings.description: DBED had not established proper controls over its purchasing transactions and user access for FMIS disbursements, allowing employees to process purchases without independent approval or improper access without detection. During fiscal year 2014, $118.1 million in disbursements were processed through FMIS.

dollar_amounts.context: total disbursements processed through FMIS during fiscal year 2014
maximum threshold for purchase orders without independent approval in two departments
purchase orders processed by four employees without independent approval during audit period
purchase orders approved by one employee without reviewing supporting documentation
small procurement purchase orders approved by second employee without reviewing supporting documentation

findings.recommendation: a. establish consistent independent online approval requirements so that purchase orders for all departments exceeding $5,000 are subject to such approval; b. ensure that adequate supporting documentation is reviewed by employees responsible for approving purchase orders; c. ensure that appropriate supervisory personnel monitor employee security profiles in FMIS for consistency with employee job responsibilities.
